touches.text: Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).
PURPOSE: The system's notary: runs proofs and seals their verdicts.

WHY: Law 8: nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and the verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide. A green cannot be self-granted. A machine under CodeMother, not a device: CodeMother does not build, so the tester inside her puts no builder between a build and its verdict, and nothing here needs its own process in the rack, since each proof run is its own process already.
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#90 (a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal, measured 2026-11-12): "then we have to invent a way for seals to be host independent. one way would be to create a sealing machine in cairn. there's only ever one cairn until we have a laptop die and have to fail over to a backup".
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machine build_inspector; db client.
VERBS: run, notices, CodeMother's verbs reached over the bus (RULE 1). COMMANDS: cairn codemother test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, ...), shortcut cairn test; proofgate (the hook: proofs run by hand).

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
